... SECOND INNINGS ...

India now come out to bat for the first time in the match with England sitting of 353 runs. The Indian batters have been in good form in the series, especially Yashasvi Jaiswal. The task in hand can be a tough one as the wicket is still favoring the bowlers from time to time. What is going to be India's reply? Let's find out as the Second session starts soon.

Joe Root, once again proving his mettle on Indian soil, anchored the innings with a splendid knock of 122 runs off 274 balls not out, exhibiting unwavering concentration and skill throughout his stay at the crease. His innings was not only a display of individual brilliance but also marked by crucial partnerships with the middle and lower-order batters. Particularly noteworthy was his alliance with Ollie Robinson, who notched up his maiden Test fifty, contributing significantly to England's cause before falling to Ravindra Jadeja earlier today. In addition to Root's heroics, Ben Foakes played a pivotal role in stabilizing the innings alongside his captain yesterday, ensuring that England capitalized on the opportunities presented to them after the early setbacks.

As the dust settles on the first innings of this Test match, England, having won the toss and elected to bat, have showcased their resilience and determination by posting a commendable total of 353 runs on the board. Despite a shaky start, with the scoreboard reading 110/5 in the first session yesterday, the visitors orchestrated a remarkable recovery, largely thanks to the masterclass displayed by their seasoned campaigner, Joe Root.

Root's innings was a testament to his resilience and class, as he meticulously constructed his century throughout 226 deliveries, guiding England away from the early troubles they faced at 112-5. The afternoon session saw a more cautious approach from England, as they focused on rebuilding their innings, with Root and Foakes adding 113 crucial runs for the sixth wicket. However, as the day progressed, the spotlight shifted to India's bowlers, particularly the skipper Rohit Sharma, who will be eager to dismiss Root and his resilient partner Ollie Robinson (31*) early on, as they aim to wrap up England's innings swiftly. The contrasting narratives of debutant Akash Deep's promising start and Root's masterful display have set the stage for an enthralling continuation of the contest.

Good morning and welcome to the start of Day 2 of the fourth Test between India and England here in Ranchi. After a captivating display of cricket on the opening day, we find ourselves on the precipice of another day filled with excitement and anticipation. Joe Root, silenced his critics with a magnificent century, his 31st in Test cricket, rescuing his team from a precarious position to finish the day unbeaten on 106. His partnership with Ben Foakes steadied the ship after a rocky start, propelling England to 302 for 7 at stumps.
... DAY 2, FIRST SESSION ...

Right then, that concludes an enthralling Day 1 of this Test match. England showcased resilience and determination. They will aim to capitalize on their momentum and post a competitive total, while India will seek to make quick inroads and restrict the visitors. Day 2 will begin on 24th February, Saturday, at 9:30 am IST (4 am GMT), but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

The debutant and the pick of the bowlers for India, Akash Deep is up for a chat. He talks about being very comfortable on the field today. He says that he was not worried about his debut and was only looking to play good cricket. He further adds that the Zak Crawley wicket off the NO BALL was very heartbreaking for him but getting him out the second time was even better. Ends by saying that the wicket is turning slow and it's gonna be very tough to play the spinners on a surface like this in the coming days.

In the third session, England adopted a slightly different approach, with Ben Foakes in particular adopting a more aggressive stance. The partnership between him and Joe Root flourished, surpassing the 100-run mark. However, Foakes's attacking approach ultimately led to his dismissal, depriving him of a well-deserved fifty. Tom Hartley's departure further compounded England's woes, but Root remained resolute at the crease, defying the Indian bowlers with his unwavering determination. Undeterred by external scrutiny, Root silenced his critics in emphatic fashion, crafting a magnificent century to guide his team out of a precarious situation. Meanwhile, Mohammed Siraj emerged as India's key performer, redeeming himself after a lackluster first spell. Utilizing reverse swing to his advantage, Siraj shattered pivotal partnerships, effectively halting England's momentum. Jadeja should have had Ollie Robinson but the on-field umpire did not raise his finger and the hosts already used all their reviews earlier in the game. They would be a bit disappointed as after that first session, they would have expected to bowl England out before Stumps.

England displayed remarkable resilience in the post-Lunch session, staging a remarkable fightback from a precarious position of 112-5. Joe Root and Ben Foakes joined forces to anchor the innings, constructing a vital partnership worth 86 runs. Their collaboration not only steadied the ship but also marked the first session in which England remained unscathed, a testament to their tenacity and determination. Root, in particular, showcased his class with a well-earned half-century, ably supported by Foakes, who complemented his captain's efforts with a composed batting display. Despite facing a challenging pitch and disciplined bowling from India, the English duo exhibited commendable composure and resilience. Although the Indian bowlers created some opportunities, they were unable to break the partnership before Tea.

It was a captivating first session of Test cricket dominated by the debutant, Akash Deep, who showcased his talent with the ball for India. Despite an unfortunate overstep denying him a wicket, he remained composed and struck twice in quick succession to remove Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope. His disciplined bowling kept the English batters under pressure throughout the session. Ravindra Jadeja and Ravichandran Ashwin complemented Akash Deep well, claiming a wicket each to dent England's early progress. Winning the toss, England opted to bat but faced early setbacks as their openers struggled against the Indian bowlers. Although Joe Root provided stability with a solid inning, Zak Crawley's departure after a promising start and Ben Stokes' dismissal just before Lunch further hindered England's momentum.

England concludes Day 1 with a commanding position in the Test match! Joe Root's magnificent century, his 31st in Tests and 10th against India which is the highest for any player against the hosts stood out as the highlight of the day. Ending the day unbeaten on 106 runs, Root led the charge for England alongside Ollie Robinson, aiming to further bolster their already imposing total. While India made early breakthroughs in the first session courtesy of an exceptional spell from the debutant, Akash Deep, they couldn't capitalize on the momentum and will need to regroup and refine their strategies ahead of Day 2.

With Joe Root still at the crease on 16 runs, England will be pinning their hopes on their most experienced batter to anchor the innings and steer them out of troubled waters. However, with the Indian bowling lineup firing on all cylinders, the visitors find themselves facing an uphill battle as they look to salvage their innings in the subsequent sessions of the day. Join us back at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) for the start of the Second Session on Day 1 of this Test match.

The session belonged emphatically to debutant Akash Deep, who announced his arrival on the Test stage in spectacular fashion by dismantling the top three of England's batting lineup. His fiery spell, accounting for the prized scalps of Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, and Ollie Pope, set the tone for India's dominance early on, leaving the visitors on the back foot from the outset. Despite a brief resurgence led by Jonny Bairstow and Joe Root, who stitched together a resilient partnership of 52 runs, England's batting order struggled to counter the relentless onslaught from the Indian bowlers. The brilliance of Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja further compounded England's woes, with the former claiming the crucial wicket of Bairstow through a brilliant review by skipper Rohit Sharma, while the latter dismissed the English captain Ben Stokes in the final over before lunch.

PITCH REPORT - Graeme Swann is pitchside. He says that he has not seen anything like this and it is like a dry riverbed. Adds that there are a lot of cracks on it and the spinners might get turn from very early in the game. Says it is a batting first surface. Deep Dasgupta joins him and says that there is a tinge of grass on it and the cracks would open up but it will be a slow turner. Mentions there will be not much bite on it and it could play better than expected.

Rohit Sharma, at the toss interview, says that they would have batted first as well as the wicket looks dry and is going to work well for the spinners. He adds that the young players in the team are stepping up already and have performed really well which is a good sign for the team. He talks about the debutants in the previous game and how well they have performed. He ends by saying that Jasprit Bumrah is rested for this game and Akash Deep gets his Test Debut for India.

Ben Stokes, at the toss interview, says that they will bat first. Adds that going 2-1 down makes this an important one but every game is in this series. He says that the pitch looks very dry and he has learnt that if you win the toss in India you bat first. Mentions that they have to adjust to the conditions and adapt well and counter the pace assistance in the first hour. Says that the bowling has been good and there is a schedule but a lot of work to do to get ready. Ends by saying he is happy with how they have operated throughout the series. Informs they have made a couple of changes as Mark Wood has been rested and Ollie Robinson comes in for him while Shoaib Bashir replaces Rehan Ahmed.
